key_insight: M$^3$-Gen generates biologically coherent gene expression profiles from histopathology images plus clinical metadata, while also highlighting which image regions influenced the output.
clinical_relevance: This could help expand multimodal cancer research when gene expression data are limited, expensive, or difficult to share, without relying on direct molecular profiling for every case.
method: Learns a shared latent representation from clinical variables and pathology images using contrastive learning.
Conditions a GAN on the fused multimodal embeddings to synthesize gene expression profiles.
Uses attention to provide intrinsic interpretability by linking output to influential image regions.
evidence_signal: In TCGA evaluations, the model produced realistic and functionally meaningful gene expression data.
watch_item: The approach is promising for research, but real-world deployment will need careful validation for dataset shift, generalizability, and whether generated profiles are sufficiently reliable for downstream use.
paper_title: M$^3$-Gen: Interpretable Multimodal Generation of Gene Expression Profiles Using Clinical and Imaging Data
